###Understanding the type of statement

We are given an $\maroonC{\text{OR}}$ statement. A certain $x$-value is a solution of the statement if it satisfies ***either*** of the inequalities.

Therefore, the solution of this statement is the ***union*** of the solutions of both inequalities. In other words, the entire collection of the solutions of both inequalities forms the solution of this statement.

###Finding the solutions to the two inequalities

The solution of the first inequality,  $5x-29> -34$, is $x>-1$. [[☃ explanation 1]]

The solution of the second inequality,  $2x+31<29$, is $x<-1$.

The inequalities $\tealD{x>-1}$ and $\purpleD{x<-1}$ are graphed below.



[[☃ image 1]]

The union of the solutions of both inequalities is all $x$-values  that are less than $-1$ along with all $x$-values that are greater than $-1$. 

This can be mathematically represented  as $x<-1$ $\text{ OR }$ $x>-1$.

*We can also think of the solution as all real values of $x$ except for $x=-\textit{1}$.*
